I got this game because it appears to be a remake of an old browser game I use to play to death that isn't available anymore. Although I wish to still play the original if possible, this remake is still a fun game and I can appreciate the more fleshed out mechanics. As advertised, a lot of this game is randomized. I initially found this to be a little frustrating, as circumstances are guaranteed to be against your favor at some point, but once I got experience with the mechanics and items the game becomes a really tight, dynamic, and enjoyable experience. It's very satisfying getting through a stage dodging enemies by using nothing but well timed explosives in the levels where getting a weapon isn't available, for example. 

That being said, there was a really elegant simplicity to the original I remember that isn't quite here. This version is cool for sure, but it doesn't quite scratch the same itch for me. There's also a few enemy designs that were either scrapped or retooled into the new ones that I quite liked, and only dealing with two enemy types at a time doesn't feel the same. I feel some of the more powerful weapons were also rebalanced a little. I can understand, but with randomized weapons that disappear when you run out of ammo I think it wouldn't have hurt to allow a few weapons to make you feel invincible for a bit. Especially with a game like this that's aiming to be exciting, it kind of just feels like the game is stopping you from having too much fun. These are minor things though, and probably have good reasons for being so. This game is good simple fun and delivers on its premise.

Some have supposed that, by its own self-defining limitations, the single-screen platformer (SSP) was doomed to fade. Indeed, by the early 2000s, what more could be accomplished within the quaint constraints of a 4:3 display? But such restrictions did offer one advantage: it forced designers to maximize every gameplay mechanic and onscreen pixel to provide the most compelling experience possible. Such is the case with Super Mutant Alien Assault, an SSP that, despite lacking those fancy scrolling graphics, provides a fulfilling quest comparable to a modern rogue-lite.

In fact, that’s exactly what this game is—a rogue-lite squeezed into a screen. Players control a squat robot that must liberate three fleets of fleeing starships—the remnants of humanity—from a host of nefarious aliens. This means jumping, gunning, and running through each of the armada's four vessels, an overall twelve ship/stage gauntlet of cramped quarters and spastic action. Once the boss alien of a fleet is defeated, the little robot avatar teleports to the next armada and begins another 4-round challenge. Completing the twelfth stage unlocks a higher difficulty for those who still have nerves to burn.

Three key mechanics distinguish Assault from its SSP peers. The first is that survivalist bent; take too many hits and the little hero explodes, forcing an abrupt do-over. Fortunately, repeated attempts unlock new weapons and abilities, some of which can be pre-equipped for the next run.

The more interesting distinction, however, is Assault’s level variety. While the overall objective—enemy elimination—never deviates, the impediments to achieving that goal often do. Some stages require the player to play courier, carrying fuel canisters and data spheres to their respective compartments before the level’s minions can be permanently eliminated. Other times, players must scurry between energy valves, releasing the building pressure before they overload and sheer the screen with an inescapable death-blast.

But the game’s unusual weapon system is what most will like or despise. Until the droid accesses a weapon station, he's defenseless. But these depots bear a hidden cruelty, their random firearm deliveries often sticking the player with a less-than-optimal loadout. Grenade launchers are great for the bigger meanies, but a miss means an out-of-control, ricocheting explosive now equally lethal to the player. Doubly-so for the rocket launcher, which must be fired from afar lest the player get caught in the resulting explosion--a likely outcome for a single-screen game. And the sniper rifle’s reload is so slow, only the most accurate marksmen will find it useful. A separate depot offers a variety of grenades that are bestowed in similar random fashion, again reinforcing that risk versus reward mentality. Players will simply have to master every type of weapon if they hope to survive.

Or maybe not. Secondary weapons and abilities, from a reusable chakram to a double-jump, can also be procured, giving players a bit more lee-way in their tactics and options. But there’s no denying Assault’s savagery: the enemies are always mutating into harsher, stronger forms. The weapons deplete fast and can’t be replaced immediately. Maneuverability is often stifled by the stage’s stuffed, unforgiving spaces. And extra abilities are helpful but not always available. Super Mutant Alien Assault is defined, more than anything, by its traitorous double-edged sensibilities.

Which is to say—this is a platformer that puts the “roguelike” first, tossing out the genre’s usual whimsy for a decidedly more “hardcore” experience. But in truth, are games like Bubble Bobble or Snow Bros. any less brutal? Cutesy pretensions aside, these were games notoriously rough on a player's sanity...and his wallet. Bubble Bobble has 100 levels, after all. Assault has twelve.

No, the game’s biggest issue is not the abundant challenge, but a lack of a certain charisma. Mechanically, the game is fine. But visually, the proceedings lack the genre's usual zest and sense of flair. Almost always, the most memorable SSPs have a likable protagonist and, often, a slate of ambient backgrounds and a catchy score. The nondescript grimness of Assault’s aesthetics and backdrops do it no favors...and its musical score is more scratchy than catchy.

But considering the current dearth of SSPs in the marketplace, Assault stands as a worthwhile addition to the genre. If not a classic, it’s certainly a valid proof-of-concept that the single-screen platformer is far from done.

Someday, just maybe, that single-screen renaissance will finally come.

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME ON PC.

THE .EXE DOES NOT RUN PROPERLY ON PC.

Game does not run properly as Gamemaker Studio (the engine this game is coded in) has issues with CPU timings, where it will speed up or delay framerate based on an internal clock that you cannot edit without opening the program in Gamemaker Studio. This is a known issue with pretty much every build of Gamemaker Studio and the few work arounds include forcing V-Sync on the game file through your graphics card settings and by locking your monitor to 60hz to force the game to run at 60fps, though this does not work for every system.

The long and short of it is that the PC build does not run the way it was meant to on most machines and the workarounds to fix the issue don't work all the time.

If you have a console, play it there as it works fine over there. As far as I'm aware, this game is available on Playstation, Xbox and Switch. When it works, it works great and is a whole lot of fun, though in its current state I cannot recommend you play this game on PC.

Initial impression and final judgement: A slower, not-as-fun, clone of Super Crate Box with a more interesting visual style. 

This game would be a real hit if it was faster, had an actual score, rewarded skill better, and was more intuitive. This review will be focusing on comparing it to Super Crate Box. 

Pros:
- Lots of interesting gameplay and weapons
- Art style is beautiful

Cons:
- not fast-paced at all, and the game lags at certain points as well, even with a beefy computer. 
- The movement and combat is too slow and floaty, not inherently pleasant to play with
- swapping weapons from the box is a less fun version of Super Crate Box's random weapons from crates
- music does NOT match the gameplay or feeling, it is much faster and more intense, which the gameplay is not
- there's no inherent reward or valuable score, at least one that I know of. You get unlocks just for completing levels, not through skill. There's no reward for improving skill aside from getting a little farther, I don't feel inclined or rewarded for getting better
- everything that is unlocked is hidden from the player -- it is not a character or weapon you can choose, but just kind of expanding the mechanics / introducing them like a tutorial. You get "fake unlocks" of mechanics/features/modes by playing the tutorial which isn't that fun, I'd rather unlock more modes just by playing and achieving things or getting high scores, rather than it just happening for no reason or part of a tutorial. 
- needlessly complex with a lot of different objectives and machines every level, or a mix of them per level, which makes the gameplay unfocused, and unintuitive 
- Unlocking new enemies to fight and the machine which buffs enemies over time -- Why? It doesn't make sense to me, and isn't rewarding to unlock more enemies. They should just appear in harder areas.

공격 수단은 총, 수류탄, 특수 능력이 있다. 이 중 특수 능력은 적을 죽였을 시 일정 확률로 떨어뜨리는 충전재를 먹고 그 수 만큼 사용할 수 있는 필살기 개념이다. 총과 수류탄의 보급방법은 좀 특이하다. 스테이지 내 총과 수류탄을 보급 받을 수 있는 기계가 있다. 그 기계로 가서 상호작용 키를 누르면 보급 받아 사용할 수 있다. 총과 수류탄 종류가 많은데 그 중 랜덤하게 하나를 받을 수 있다. 그런데 보급받은 무기들은 한 스테이지를 깨는데 충분하지 않아서 계속해서 보급 기계로 가 공급 받아야한다. 좀 귀찮을 때도 있지만 그래도 시스템적으로 자연스럽게 움직임을 발생하게하고 다양한 무기를 쓸수 있게 해주어 개인적으론 꽤 새로웠고 재미있는 시스템으로 느껴졌다. 그 외 대쉬나 회피 등을 사용할 수 있는 다양한 방어 아이템도 게임 중에 획득할 수 있다. 이러한 총, 수류탄, 특수능력, 방어 아이템들은 해금 요소이다. 아마 스테이지를 깬 횟수에 따라 해금되는 것 같다. 해금 요소에서 특이한 점으론 적도 해금된다. 꽤 걸리지만 보스도 해금된다; 즉 게임을 하면 할수록 적이 다양해진다. 아래에서 언급하겠지만 게임 볼륨 자체는 굉장히 작은편은데 이러한 요소를 조금은 메꿔준다. 다소 과하게 오래 걸리는 느낌이긴 하지만.. 조금 이상한 점은 총이나 수류탄은 맘에 안들면 보급 기계를 통해 바꾸면 되지만 다른 특수 아이템은 한번 얻으면 그 게임에선 바꾸질 못한다. 왜 이렇게 했는지 모르겠다.

BGM이 굉장히 좋고 픽셀 그래픽도 상당한 수준이다. 그 외 조작감 같은것도 흠잡을 것 없다. 앞에서 해금 요소가 있다했는데 내가 얼만큼 해금했고 다음 해금요소는 뭔지 그런 정보를 메뉴에서 볼 수 없어 아쉽다. 한글화는 되어 있지 않지만 필요성은 느끼지 못했다. 난이도는 시스템만 좀 적응되면 중간정도로 대부분이 무난하게 즐길 수 있는 수준이다.

치명적인 단점이 있는데 게임 전체 볼륨이 적다. 3개의 큰 지역이 있고 한 지역당 4개의 스테이지가 있다. 각 지역 당 마지막 스테이지는 보스가 나온다. 즉 전체 스테이지는 12개이며 이 중 3개가 보스 스테이지이다. 한 스테이지를 깨는데 걸리는 시간도 짧은 편이라 처음에 영 익숙치 않아서 여러번 다시하곤 했음에도 전체를 다 깨는데 1시간이면 충분했다. 아마 게임에 굉장히 익숙해지면 전체 다 깨는데 20분이 채 안걸리지 않을까 싶다. 이러한 적은 볼륨을 메꾸기 위해 앞서 말한 해금 시스템이 조금은 도움이 된다. 무기만 해금했다면 좀 지루했겠지만 적도 해금되면서 같은 스테이지임에도 확연히 다른 분위기가 나타나기도 하다. 맵 또한 한 지역 내에선 조금씩 돌아가며 나오는듯 하다. 스테이지마다 요구되는 미션이 다르기 때문에 맵이 달라지는것도 미미하게 효과가 있긴하다. 또한 다양한 난이도가 있어 익숨해짐에 따라 난이도를 높여가며 즐길 수 있고 3개 지역을 다 깨고 그냥 클리어되는게 아닌 다시 1 지역으로 돌아가 즐기는 엔드리스 모드도 있긴하다. 그래도 결정적인 단점으로 모든 지역의 보스는 같다. 보스라도 좀 다양하게 늘려주었더라면 매 게임의 분위기를 바꾸는데 좋았을텐데 아쉽다. 이 게임의 태그 중 Action Roguelike가 있는데 로그라이크라 보기엔 좀.. 매 맵이 조금씩 로테이션 되고 적과 아이템은 좀 랜덤하긴하나 많이 한정적이고 상술한것처럼 보스가 거의 정해져있어서 그런 느낌이 나진 않는다.그냥 단방향 아케이드 게임이라 생각해야한다.

「アーケードスタイル+ローグライク+２Dアクション」

・大まかな内容
宇宙船に乗った突然変異し続けるエイリアンを打ち倒すべく、四体のロボット達が立ち向かう。
正直物語とかないようなものです。
一つのギャラクシーに3エリア+ボスエリアで4エリアあり、三つのギャラクシーを達成すればクリアとなる。
エリアをクリアし続けることでレベルが上昇し、一定のレベルを得ることによって武器やアビリティ、雑魚からボスまですべて順々にアンロックされる仕組みになっている。

・初めに
基本的に敵を一定時間倒しきることが目的であるが、エリア別で他に行うことがある。
◇ カプセルが突出しエネルギーを蓄積しだすが、必要以上蓄積される前にクールダウンさせること。
◇ エネルギーカプセル or ボールを一定数運び、制御盤みたいなものにセットすること。
尚難易度別でカプセルの個数が違ってくる。

エリア内には武器や爆発物をランダムに生成してくれる機器が一つずつ設置されており、回復機器の場合は使用回数も制限されている(使用回数も難易度別で違ってくる)。
武器や爆発物の生成は、一定時間リチャージされることにより再度生成できる。
そのためランダムで武器や爆発物をとっかえひっかえして戦うはめになる。
毎回プレイヤーは取得した武器に応じて適応していかなければならない。
もちろんエリアの構造も変化するため、コツを掴むまではトライアンドエラーが求められる。

・戦闘に関して
かなりアグレッシブでパワフルな武器が多く使い勝手が良いものから悪いものまで、品揃えは良いがあまりにも差がありすぎる。爆発兵器が多いため武器の使いどころには注意しなければならない。
一回使えばずっと爆発し続けているチャクラムやジェットパックのジェット噴射など、アタリとハズレを楽しめられると考えられれば楽しいのかもしれないが、正直進めていくことが困難になる。
操作性は至って良好で、アビリティを利用した回避行動も大変融通が利く。2Dアクションが好きな人は安くなったあたりにやってみるといいかも。
ただ、協力プレイはカオス極まりない。1エリアに一台ある武器と爆発物の機器を二人で使うことや、熱くなり過ぎて手榴弾やC4など狭いエリアに置きまくられれば堪ったもんじゃない。起動式の大型爆弾を転がされれば避けようもない。本気でやろうと思うと厳しいかなと思います。

・気になった点
システム上印象には残らない。
敵を倒すことによってレベルが上がりパラメータや武器が増えて、それ相応にエリア別で敵のランクも任意で上げることができたら良かった。そうなるとギャラクシー数も足りないと感じる。
爆発兵器が多く、またエリアが狭いため協力には不向き。一定以上の2Dアクションの腕が必要。

・結論
セールの時に323円で購入したので、この値段なら買って損はないかと思います。一人で一周か二周クリアし、協力でギャーギャー叫んで終わるような作品です。遊べば遊ぶほどアンロックされるので、早めにクリアする方が敵の種類が増えなくて楽かもしれません。正直面白いかというと一歩手前で難しいところ。一応ハードまでクリアできたと考えたら、遊べた作品なのかもしれません。

IN A NUTSHELL:
[i]Super Mutant Alien Assault is a frantic roguelite with a huge selection of weapons and items, all wrapped up in a beautiful pixel art package and made even better by the addition of couch co-op.[/i]



I'm told that Super Mutant Alien Assault is a lot like Super Crate Box, but since I haven't played SCB (and maybe you haven't either), I'll give you a quick rundown on the idea of Super Mutant Alien Assault:

The game is broken down into 3 zones (each comprised of 3 regular levels followed by a boss fight).  Every level randomly presents you with one of a handful objectives ranging from surviving until a timer runs out, to shutting off devices before they catastrophically overheat, to retrieving fuel rods from one part of the map and depositing them in another location.  Along the way, you're beset by a variety of enemies (the titular aliens) and, true to form, "game over" is a single death away.

Fortunately, you'll have access to a generous array of unlockable weapons and items scattered throughout the game--and this, in my opinion, is where the game shines.  The sheer variety of weapons and items may be impressive, but the fact that they're generally well-balanced is shocking--particularly when you consider how diverse they are.  There's the shotgun with its typical buckshot spread, the sniper rifle that pierces multiple targets, a laser that becomes more powerful as it fires, and...an electric pogo stick?  

Yet you'll discover combinations and quirks that aren't immediately obvious.  Orbs ordinarily prevent you from firing your weapons while you carry them, but if you're using that electric pogo stick, you're still able to kill enemies...because the pogo works by dropping down on their heads (plus it lets you move faster!)  The explosive boomerang will injure you if it's still armed when it returns...but if you're nimble, you can kite it around indefinitely, letting it chew up enemies as you run around with your sidearm.  The "Mega Chakra" is a sloppy and temperamental thing, yet even after being abandoned for another weapon, it'll violently react to enemy contact.

And that's to say nothing of all the sidearms, explosives, defensive items, special abilities, and perks the game has to offer.  Hacking modules, a transforming blaster for a sidearm, remote satchel charges, a radioactive unit that passively accumulates the resource used for special abilities, teleporters, forcefields, etc.  The point is that there's a great variety of tools at your disposal, and many complement each other in unexpected ways.  Since each player can hold a primary weapon, sidearm, explosive, special ability, defensive ability, and perk at any given time, the combinations and strategies are surprisingly vast.  Perhaps not quite "Binding of Isaac" levels, but great nonetheless.

There's a commendable ecology of enemies, as well, bolstered by the game's mutation mechanic:  Smaller, weaker alien variations will grow into monstrous versions if exposed to too much radiation (the result of leaving them alive for too long while radioactive beacons are spilling green light everywhere) or if they pick up the green radiation pellets that drop as ammo for special abilities.  In other words, if an enemy beats the player to the pellet, not only do they begin mutating into a more powerful version of themselves, but the player is denied a valuable resource.   It's a refreshing dynamic and forces a balance between hoovering up pellets despite your tank being full, and leaving them until you need them (but risking the chance that they benefit an enemy instead). 

At the lowest difficulty, the game is appropriately easy; on the hardest, the average player won't be able to sleepwalk through a run (sleeprun?).  And despite getting killed a lot at higher difficulties, I can't recall any moments where I felt like the game cheated me.

Of course, if you're still having trouble, the couch co-op allows two players to tackle all 12 levels together on one screen.  Combined with the aforementioned abundance of strange and novel items, this feature makes for some intense and hilarious moments that really amplify the game's crazier side.

I really wanted to like this game, I honestly really did. As somebody who loved super crate box, I've been looking for a single screen puzzle-shooter to top it since. And well, SMAA is almost a contender. Almost.

Touting itself as "The Citzen Kane of Super Crate Box Clones", joke or not, admittedly got my expectations up. The gameplay looked promising from the trailers, so I decided to pounce on it immediately. While the hype and love started oozing from every one of my pores as soon as I started playing, the well dried up pretty fast of my enjoyment. There seems to be a soulless void... an emptiness, to this game. And, I'm dedicating the rest of the review to try and figure it out for myself using self-talk therapy.

Firstly the positives:

The graphics are very good. The gibs of the enemies are crunchy, and remind me a lot of shooting a rocket or super shotgun at some cacodemons in doom. It's very satisfying when you chunk a cluster of flying enemies with a rocket launcher, or snipe a particularly troublesome foe in the head with a sniper rifle. The spaceship's designs are all very pretty, and every enemy is thought out aesthetically to match their obvious functions.

The gimmicks it's added to distance itself from crate box are also unique and interesting. Monsters mutate not only in speed, but now in function- they grow larger, gain extra abilities, and sometimes can even reach more than one stage. There are now grenades and special abilities added to the mix, which can be powered by the radiation gathered from upgraded monsters. This means you can choose to upgrade some monsters for some special ability ammo if you wish! There are different types of levels, making your goal from each vary.

But now for the negatives:

After deliberating the issue with SMAA in my head, I've realized it all comes down to the game's speed. A game like this doesn't need to be fast to be enjoyable, but when a game is both fast and slow at the same time the action begins to clash and create friction between the different elements. 

To sum it up in an allegory: Super Mutant Alien Assault is like making Usain Bolt hit a huge rock with a pickaxe. You can sprint around the rock smashing it all you want, but at the end of the day, you're doing long tedious work and have to keep running around in circles to get the job done. In super crate box, you shoot fast, deal lots of damage, but die fast. This is because super crate box is a high score based arcade game, so it's just skill that lets you get further. However, SMAA has changed the genre to sort of a roguelike room clearing game, and has to be rebalanced to fit that. Therefore, this fast movement based game has now been refitted to pump in more gimmicks, include player health bars, ways to stall, more player power... And to balance it out, more enemy health. Now the game runs a whole lot slower, and since the movement is about the same, feels a whole lot clunkier as a result. Sound familiar?

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aXQ2lO3ieBA

To quickly wrap up the other things I have problems with:

The music needs to calm down. This is a minor gripe because I can just mute it, but based on the new speed of the game... Loud aggressive dubstep music just doesn't work. It sounds like every second of my game should just be some call of duty montage on youtube, even if I'm just sitting around waiting for enemies to spawn. I just muted it after a while. This is pretty much personal opinion and I don't factor it into my review, but thought I should mention it.

The slowdown effects are tied to framerate. That means that whenever the game wants to dramatically slow down time, it reduces the framerate directly. This is extremely distracting, and text cannot justify how much it hurts to look at. I don't know if the engine itself is responsible for this, but I seriously hope it will be patched eventually.

Overall, while not all terrible, I still cannot recommend SMAA because I find Super Crate Box to be way more enjoyable for free instead of 8 dollars. If this game was the first of it's kind with nothing to compare to, maybe I'd say it's worth the price, but honestly there have been games that have done it better before for lower prices and/or free.

[h1]tl;dr[/h1] Super Mutant Alien Assault is an unashamed Super Crate Box clone, and with good reason: it's every bit as addicting as it's paragon, but adds it's own twists.

[h1]words[/h1]
Super Mutant Alien Assault is an arcade platformer shooter, where you play a tiny robot combating an onslaught of mutant aliens. The controls are solid (the only gripe I have is not being able to remap the d-pad to make the pad controls mimic the keyboard controls), the graphics are [b]excellent[/b] some of the best art I've seen in a long while. The music is okay and the sounds are passable.

The levels have a nice amount of variety without having "bad levels" that you wish you won't get. There are a variety of "modes" for the levels ranging from just surviving a set amount of time to transferring fragile gas canisters to a receptacle elsewhere on the level. As you play, you unlock more game modes, enemies, weapons and power-ups.

You get weapons, explosives and health from vending machines, that take a while to recharge, and sometimes levels spawn with crates containing pick-ups that range from granting you defensive moves, to just plain health pick-ups.
The game has a bunch of interesting mechanics, like the towers that power up enemies when they activate, making the enemies larger and more dangerous, but large enemies also drop ammunition for your super attack, which you can receive from crates.

Bottom line, I almost passed on Super Mutant Alien Assault, but I'm [b]so[/b] happy I decided to take a chance on it because of the appealing visual style, it's a very good game. If you're wary about Early Access, the devs plans seem to be to basically just add more levels, enemies and items and to tweak balance, ie. the game is basically feature complete. If the trailer or screenshots look at all interesting to you, or if you enjoyed Super Crate Box, I definitely recommend  checking Super Mutant Alien Assault out.

Super Mutant Alien Assault

TL;DR: SMAA doesn't do anything particularly original, but what it does do is polished to a glowing shine. Still in early access, the cons are compensated for by the pros. Recommended for those who enjoy a challange or over the top mindless gunplay.


Pros
1. Gorgeous flowing pixel art style
2. Controls are crisp and tight
3. Excellent weapon variery and distinction

Cons
1. Lack of online co-op
2. The game feels a little short


Pro 1: Gorgeous flowing pixel art style
SMAA is presented in a high quality pixel art style that evokes the feel of classic 16-bit games. Like other games of a similar style, such as Bleed, Shovel Knight, and They Bleed Pixels, SMAA's art style works well with the game design. Every alien's design is distinct and it is easy to distinguish an interactable item from background scenery.  

Pro 2: Controls are crisp and tight
SMAA shines in its control scheme. The options allow for keyboard control, and native support for XBOX controllers or gamepads with X mode support. The majority of controls are rebindable to your own comfort. The robots respond perfectly to your commands, with no noticable lag or over/understeering. They attack when you tell them, and move where you direct. Given the game's frantic nature, a tight smooth control scheme is a necessity, and SMAA delivers perfectly. When you make a mistake, you will not be able to blame poor controls.

Pro 3: Excellent weapon variery and distinction
A major component of SMAA is the selection of weapons avaliable for your use. With weapons ranging from a simple short ranged shiv to pistols, AK-47 assault rifles, miniguns, grenades, to exotic unique ones like the plasma pogostick, every weapon comes with its own strengths and weaknesses, but most importantly, they all feel unique. Shotguns have spread effects, sniper rifles can pierce through multiple aliens at once. The more you play the game, the more weapons are unlocked for use. Special abilities and defence moves round out your combat skills, giving you the tools to handle even the largest boss fights.


Con 1: Lack of online co-op
SMAA's greatest flaw is its lack of LAN or online co-op support. Only local co-op is supported, meaning that both players must be physically present in order to play. While this is not a major issue for those who enjoy such activities with friends, Online co-op would provide greater variety and competition.

2. The game feels a little short
SMAA has four main gameplay modes spread out across 12 levels. Each level takes 1-2 minutes to complete, so a full playthrough of all 3 galaxies can be done in about 20 minutes. While great for the causal player, those who are looking to unlock everything will quickly find themselves playing through the same stages and fighting the same bosses over and over. Increasing the number of potential boss creatures, or randomizing the order in which you encounter them would help to reduce repetition.


Conclusions
Overall, SMAA is a perfect example of a small team indy game developed with a clear goal in mind. So long as it's fun and enjoyable, it doesn't have to offer a unique game experience, and SMAA delivers on the promise of fun. Tightly focused, it knows what it wants to achieve and sets out to do it without adding in excess baggage. 

Highly recommended when on sale.
